- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for 3–7d horizon.
- If supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates downside risk; add 3–8% downward buffer for 30d forecasts.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and supply net is negative, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 3–5d moving average of true prices.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model often overreacts to recent auctions; cap forecast increase to 3–5% above recent 7d average.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model underestimates drop; apply upward bias correction by 5–10% for 30d forecasts.
- When sentiment is bullish but supply net is negative, model often fails to account for policy lag; delay forecast peak by 3–5 days and reduce magnitude by 10–15%.
